blockers.quote: Night thirty. Eight hours out here against 8,760 in there (c03). Every night, for a month. More than ninety-nine of every hundred hours you've lived this month happened in there.
blockers.why: Arithmetic slip against row c03: at 1,000 times human speed, a year of 8,760 hours inside corresponds to 8.76 hours outside (about eight and three-quarter hours), not 8 hours. Eight hours outside at 1,000x speed yields only 8,000 hours inside. Stating 'Eight hours out here against 8,760 in there' contradicts the ledger row's own calculation ('8,760 / 1,000 = 8.76 h is our arithmetic').
blockers.fix: Night thirty. About eight and three-quarter hours out here against 8,760 in there (c03). Every night, for a month. More than ninety-nine of every hundred hours you've lived this month happened in there.

blockers.quote: The hard ones take about 2,200 class hours at the diplomats' school (c26). You've had seven years of evenings. Four languages, at a working level.
blockers.why: Scope overstatement: row c26 cites the Foreign Service Institute (FSI), which specifically measures class hours for native English-speaking US diplomats learning Category IV languages. Referring generally to 'the diplomats' school' without 'US' states a single country's specific training benchmark as an unqualified general finding.
blockers.fix: The hard ones take about 2,200 class hours at the US diplomats' school (c26). You've had seven years of evenings. Four languages, at a working level.

keep.quote: People dropped 31 metres into a net later judged their own fall 36% longer than other people's (c18). A moment is as long as the memory it leaves.
Why a cable? In rats, the sleeping brain replayed a learned route six to seven times faster than the run itself (c10).
Sleep is when the brain files the day (c14). And one small, famous experiment, in 1924, decided that forgetting is mostly the new rubbing out the old (c13).
